full_judgment:
3. The trial of the accused petitioner was held in absentia and he was arrested on 31.1.1994 and thereafter he filed the criminal appeal before the High Court Division out of time by 1780 days with an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act praying for condonation of delay in preferring the appeal against the judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the Assistant Judge, Chittagong on 22.2.1989 in ST Case No. 111 of 1987. The learned Judges of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order rejected the petition for condonation of delay in preferring the criminal appeal by the accused petitioner on the finding that no sufficient cause has been shown for condonation of such inordinate delay of 1780 days. 

 4. Mr. Abu Salek, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, has reiterated the same ground as was taken before the High Court Division that the petitioner having been tried without complying with the provision of section 339(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the learned Judges of the High Court Division erred in law in not condoning the delay in preferring the appeal. The learned Judges of the High Court Division have considered this submission of the learned Advocate and noticed that when the accused-petitioner was enlarged on bail after appearance in this case in Court no notification as per provision of section 339B(1) CrPC was required to be published by the trial Court. Apart from the question whether section 5 of the Limitation Act was at all available to the petitioner we find that in the absence of any sufficient cause shown for condonation of such inordinate delay in preferring the criminal appeal by the petitioner the learned Judges of the High Court Division have rightly rejected the petition under section 5 of the Limitation Act. The petition is, therefore, dismissed.
